heroData.title: EOR & PEO in El Salvador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in El Salvador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in El Salvador.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting an employment contract in Spanish is mandatory. It must specify the probation period, which is legally capped at 30 days in El Salvador.

steps.title: National ID & NIT Collection
steps.description: Collecting the employee's Unique Identity Document (DUI) and Tax Identification Number (NIT). Note that for residents, NIT is now often unified with DUI.

steps.title: ISSS & AFP Registration
steps.description: Registering the employee with the Salvadoran Social Security Institute (ISSS) and the chosen Pension Fund Administrator (AFP) within 15 days of hiring.

steps.title: Life Insurance Setup
steps.description: Arranging mandatory life insurance for employees as per Article 308 of the Labor Code (often managed via EOR provider plugins).

steps.title: Digital Gateway Setup
steps.description: Setting up internal communication and payroll portals. Most EORs provide a unified dashboard for remote workers.

rows.label: Social Security (ISSS)
values: Employer contribution capped at a salary of $1,000.

rows.label: Pension (AFP)
values: Employer contribution to the selected private pension fund.

rows.label: INSAFORP
values: Training tax for companies with 10+ employees.

rows.label: Christmas Bonus (Aguinaldo)
values: Statutory bonus paid in December based on years of service.

rows.label: Vacation Bonus
values: A 30% premium on top of the 15 days of annual paid leave.

items.title: Probation Limit
items.text: The statutory probation period is exactly 30 days. Any attempt to extend this in the contract is legally void.

items.title: 13th Month Rules
items.text: Aguinaldo must be paid between December 12th and 20th. Rates: 15 days salary (1-3 yrs), 19 days (3-10 yrs), 21 days (10+ yrs).

items.title: Severance Calculation
items.text: In El Salvador, severance for 'unjustified dismissal' typically equals 30 days of salary for each year of service, capped at a specific monthly multiplier.

items.title: Bitcoin Payroll
items.text: While Bitcoin is legal tender, Article 120 of the Labor Code requires salaries to be paid in legal currency (USD or BTC). Most employees strictly prefer USD.

items.title: Standard Hours
items.text: 44 hours per week (8 hours weekdays, 4 hours Saturday). Overtime premium is 100% (double pay).

items.title: Paid Leave
items.text: 15 days of paid annual leave after one year of continuous service.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.text: Employees are entitled to 11 mandatory paid public holidays annually.

items.title: Currency
items.text: The US Dollar (USD) is the primary currency for all payroll and business transactions.

faqs.question: Does EOR reduce Permanent Establishment (PE) risk in El Salvador?
faqs.answer: Yes, using an EOR ensures that the foreign company does not need to register a branch, significantly lowering tax nexus risks.

faqs.question: Can I hire part-time workers via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they are still entitled to pro-rated social security and Aguinaldo benefits.

faqs.question: What is the typical EOR fee?
faqs.answer: Management fees in El Salvador range from $200 to $500 per employee per month depending on the provider and volume.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Employers must provide ISSS (health) and AFP (pension) by law, plus workers' compensation coverage.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Aggregating base salary, commissions, overtime hours, and any applicable bonuses or 'Quincena 25' benefits.

steps.title: Statutory Deductions
steps.description: Applying ISSS (3.0% employee) and AFP (7.25% employee) deductions. Note the ISSS salary cap of $1,000 for deductions.

steps.title: Income Tax (ISR) Calculation
steps.description: Applying the progressive tax table to the taxable income after social security deductions. Rates range from 10% to 30%.

steps.title: Net Payment Execution
steps.description: Disbursing net salary to employees via local bank transfers. payments are usually made on a bi-monthly (every 15 days) basis.

steps.title: Regulatory Reporting
steps.description: Submitting the OIKOS (Social Security) and Ministry of Finance (Tax) reports by the 10th and 15th of the following month respectively.

items.title: Bi-Monthly Frequency
items.text: It is customary in El Salvador to pay employees twice a month (15th and 30th), though monthly payment is legally permissible.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Failing to remit ISSS/AFP payments on time can result in interest charges and being barred from certain government contracts.

items.title: The Quincena 25 Law
items.text: Ensure your payroll system accounts for the special 'Quincena 25' law which designates specific bonuses as exempt from social security and pension under certain conditions.

items.title: AFP Choice
items.text: Employees can choose between AFP Crecer or AFP Confía for their retirement fund مدیریت.

items.title: Contribution Split
items.text: Employer pays 7.75%; Employee pays 7.25%. Total 15% is deposited monthly.

items.title: Reporting Portal
items.text: All pension reporting is serialized through the UNICO software for electronic filing to the Superintendent of the Financial System.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in any currency?
faqs.answer: Legally, USD is the official currency. Bitcoin is also legal, but for tax reporting, all values must be converted to USD equivalents.

faqs.question: What happens if an employee has multiple jobs?
faqs.answer: The primary employer handles the standard deductions, but the employee is responsible for annual tax finalization.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses like Aguinaldo are subject to income tax above the legal exemption threshold (approx. 2 minimum salaries).

steps.title: Gross Base Salary
steps.description: Primary input. Must be at least the sectoral minimum wage (approx. $365 USD).

steps.title: Overtime & Commissions
steps.description: Variable inputs. Overtime hours are calculated at a 100% premium (double time).

steps.title: Tenure (Years of Service)
steps.description: Required to calculate the Aguinaldo (Christmas Bonus) bracket (1-3, 3-10, 10+ years).

steps.title: Vacation Status
steps.description: Determining if the 30% vacation bonus should be applied to the current period.

steps.title: Deduction Caps
steps.description: Ensuring the ISSS deduction does not exceed the $1,000 salary cap.

items.title: Taxable Income Base
items.text: Taxable income for ISR is calculated AFTER deducting ISSS and AFP contributions from the gross salary.

items.title: Aguinaldo Brackets
items.text: Don't forget to update the Aguinaldo logic: 15 days (1-3 yrs), 19 days (3-10 yrs), 21 days (10+ yrs).

items.title: Currency Sync
items.text: Since El Salvador uses USD, there are no FX conversion risks in the calculator unless paying from a non-USD parent company.

items.title: Net Take-Home
items.text: The final amount the employee receives after all statutory deductions.

items.title: Total Cost of Employment
items.text: Includes Gross Salary + Employer ISSS/AFP + INSAFORP + Accrued Bonuses.

items.title: Statutory Accruals
items.text: Monthly estimation of Aguinaldo and Vacation bonuses to avoid year-end cash flow shocks.

faqs.question: Does the calculator handle Bitcoin payments?
faqs.answer: The logic is identical, but the final result should be displayed in both USD and BTC using a real-time API.

faqs.question: How often do tax tables change?
faqs.answer: Rarely, but it's important to monitor the Legislative Assembly's 'Decretos' at the start of each fiscal year.

faqs.question: Can I calculate severance for redundancy?
faqs.answer: Yes, the standard is 30 days per year of service, capped at 4 minimum salaries per month of calculation.

steps.title: Company Name Clearance
steps.description: Verify availability of the corporate name at the Registry of Commerce (Registro de Comercio).

steps.title: Public Deed Execution
steps.description: A local notary must draft and certify the Articles of Incorporation (Public Deed). Requires a minimum of 2 shareholders.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit at least 5% of the initial capital (minimum $2,000 for S.A. de C.V.) into a local bank client account.

steps.title: Registry Submission
steps.description: Submit documents to MiEmpresa.gob.sv for unified registration including NRC (Tax ID), NIT, and Municipal License.

steps.title: Legal Book Legalization
steps.description: Legalizing accounting and administrative books (Shareholder Registry, Board Meetings) via an authorized auditor.

rows.label: Minimum Social Capital
values: At least 5% ($100) must be paid upfront during registration.

rows.label: Registry Fees
values: Charged based on the total capital amount.

rows.label: Legal & Notary Fees
values: Varies based on complexity and law firm seniority.

rows.label: Municipal License
values: Annual fee varying by the municipality (San Salvador vs. others).

rows.label: Commercial License
values: Initial registration with the Registry of Commerce.

items.title: S.A. de C.V. Flexibility
items.text: The Stock Company with Variable Capital is most popular for foreign investors due to ease of increasing/decreasing capital without public deed modification.

items.title: MiEmpresa Portal
items.text: Utilize the 'Ventanilla Única' at MiEmpresa.gob.sv to cut registration time from 30 days to approximately 5-7 business days.

items.title: Resident Agent
items.text: Foreign shareholders do not need to be residents, but the company must have a legal representative who is a Salvadoran resident or citizen.

items.title: S.A. de C.V.
items.text: Corporate entity with limited liability. Minimum 2 shareholders. Capital is represented by shares.

items.title: Sucursal (Branch)
items.text: Extension of a foreign parent company. Requires registration of the parent's charters and financial statements.

items.title: Limited Liability (Ltda.)
items.text: Similar to S.A. but capital is divided into quotas. Transfers require public deed amendment.

faqs.question: Can a company be 100% foreign-owned?
faqs.answer: Yes, El Salvador allows 100% foreign ownership of share capital in most sectors.

faqs.question: What is the timeline for bank account setup?
faqs.answer: Typically 2-4 weeks after the company is registered, depending on KYC requirements.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical office?
faqs.answer: Yes, a physical address is required for the Registry of Commerce and the Ministry of Finance.

steps.title: Talent Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging local platforms like Tecoloco.com and LinkedIn to source bilingual talent, especially in San Salvador and Santa Tecla.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Conducting skill-based assessments. Tech talent often undergoes English proficiency testing (TOEFL/TOEIC) for multinational roles.

steps.title: Background Verification
steps.description: Checking criminal records (Antecedentes Penales) and police records (Solvencia de la PNC), which is a standard requirement for local hiring.

steps.title: Interview & Selection
steps.description: Multi-stage interviews focusing on cultural fit and adaptability to remote or hybrid work environments.

steps.title: Offer & Contract
steps.description: Finalizing the offer letter in line with the Minimum Wage Decree (currently $365 for most sectors) and drafting the formal contract.

items.title: Growing Tech Hub
items.text: San Salvador is emerging as a 'nearshore' tech hub due to its alignment with US Central Time (CST) and high English proficiency among youth.

items.title: Recruitment Fees
items.text: Local agencies typically charge between 10% and 15% of the candidate's annual gross salary for successful placement.

items.title: 90/10 Rule
items.text: Article 7 of the Labor Code requires that at least 90% of a company's staff must be Salvadoran nationals, and they must receive at least 85% of total wages.

items.title: Principal Hubs
items.text: San Salvador (Capital), Santa Tecla, and Antiguo Cuscatlán are the primary zones for high-skilled labor.

items.title: Free Trade Zones
items.text: Many staffing firms operate within Export Processing Zones (Zonas Francas) like American Park or World Trade Center San Salvador.

items.title: University Pipelines
items.text: UCA (Universidad Centroamericana) and Don Bosco University are the top producers of engineering and CS talent.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for termination?
faqs.answer: The standard legal notice period is 15 days, although contracts often specify 30 days for senior roles.

faqs.question: Are remote workers subject to local labor laws?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are physically performing work in El Salvador, the local Labor Code applies regardless of the employer's location.

faqs.question: How long does it take to hire a senior dev?
faqs.answer: Typically 4-6 weeks from initial sourcing to contract signing in the current competitive market.

faqs.question: Can I use an HRIS to manage Aguinaldo payments?

faqs.question: Is cloud-hosting legal for employee data?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided there are adequate security measures and it doesn't violate sectoral privacy regulations.

faqs.question: Do I need to report HRIS usage to the government?
faqs.answer: No, but the *outputs* (reports) must meet government formatting standards.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: El Salvador has fully adopted IFRS (Full and for SMEs). Local statutory accounting must be maintained in Spanish and USD.

items.title: Mandatory Auditor

items.title: Fiscal Year

faqs.question: Can I keep my books in a foreign currency?
faqs.answer: No, legal books and tax filings must be expressed in US Dollars (USD).

faqs.question: How long should I keep accounting records?
faqs.answer: The statute of limitations for tax audits is generally 3-5 years, but it's recommended to keep records for 10 years.

faqs.question: Are software licenses taxable for VAT?

faqs.question: What happens if I miss an ISSS payment?

faqs.answer: Dividends sent abroad are subject to a 5% withholding tax unless a treaty provides otherwise (SV has few treaties).

faqs.question: Can I pay taxes in Bitcoin?

steps.title: Drafting in Spanish

items.title: Civil Law System
items.text: El Salvador uses a Civil Law system; written statutes and codes take precedence over previous court rulings (precedents).

items.title: Jurisdiction Issues
items.text: Foreign choices of law are often valid, but labor and tax matters always remain under the exclusive jurisdiction of Salvadoran law.

items.title: IP Protection
items.text: Register your trademarks and patents with the CNR (Registro de la Propiedad Intelectual) as protection is strictly 'First-to-file'.

items.title: Notary Role
items.text: In El Salvador, a Notary is a highly qualified lawyer who provides public faith to acts and contracts.

items.title: Force Majeure

faqs.question: Can I use DocuSign for MSAs in El Salvador?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is generally accepted, but for high-value assets or real estate, a certified 'Firma Electrónica' or physical notary is required.

faqs.question: How long do commercial disputes take?
faqs.answer: Public courts can take 2-4 years; arbitration centers usually resolve issues within 6-12 months.

faqs.question: Is non-compete enforceable?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided it is reasonable in time (usually 1-2 years), geography, and includes compensation.
